comments.body:
Read-only investigation complete. Root cause confirmed, and the severity is higher than "operational toil": this is a signing-correctness hole, not just a stale checkout.

## Root cause

The MCP code workspace (`gerrit_mcp_code`, mounted at `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`) is a persistent `main` checkout that is cloned once and thereafter only reused. No deployed path advances its working-tree HEAD. Autodeploy advances a *separate* mirror and its own deploy marker files, never this volume.

`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` defines "present" as `.git` exists plus HEAD resolves, with no freshness check at all:

- `:12` `MCP_CODE_DIR="${MCP_CODE_DIR:-/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code}"`
- `:127-130` `code_repo_present()` — tests only `[ -e "${MCP_CODE_DIR}/.git" ]` and `git -C ... rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`
- `:155-159` `clone_code_locked()` rechecks presence and returns early: "code checkout was cloned by another container"
- `:162-164` clones only when absent/unusable
- `:175-177` `provision_code()` — `if code_repo_present; then return 0`

So on every normal restart and redeploy it exits immediately, leaving HEAD wherever it was.

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` never fast-forwards the volume:

- `:399-408` launches the MCP container with `MCP_CODE_DIR` / `REBAR_ROOT` pointed at the volume and mounts `gerrit_mcp_code:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`
- `:493-497` fetches only `/var/lib/rebar/mirror`
- `:557-575` no-op ticks do pressure cleanup, MCP self-heal, retire sweep, service checks — no workspace advance
- `:801-915` MCP redeploy rsyncs the mirror into the deploy repo and rebuilds the image, but only *mounts* the pre-existing volume
- `:951-959` success advances `$SHA_FILE` / `$MCP_SHA_FILE` marker files, not the code workspace

## Gates sign against it unknowingly

The completion close path is the serious one. It pins the default ref with `_pin_completion_ref(None)` -> `resolve_ref("HEAD", fetch=False)` (`transition_close.py:128-143`), then `verify_with_auto_resume` calls `llm.verify_completion(..., source="attested", ref=(ref or "HEAD"), fetch=False, ...)` (`close_autoresume.py:271-279`). The post-verify signing drift check re-resolves *that same pinned SHA*, again without fetching (`transition_close.py:310-323`).

A stale-but-internally-consistent HEAD therefore passes the drift check and can emit a valid `completion-verifier` signature. The drift check compares the stale tree against itself, so staleness is invisible to it by construction.

Plan-review is partially protected but not authoritatively. `review_plan` and standalone `verify_completion` default to `origin/main` with `fetch=True`, so those producer paths can refresh before snapshotting. But claim-time currency is explicitly no-network: `current_head_sha` resolves the configured gate ref with `fetch=False` (`gate_source.py:89-109`), and scoped drift rehashing uses `gate_ref_hash_basis(..., fetch=False)`. Both compare against the *locally fetched idea* of `origin/main`, not the actual remote. The store-freshness machinery (`_store/freshness.py:109-169`) covers the ticket store only and never inspects `MCP_CODE_DIR`.

## Measured drift

Reflog on `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` shows clone plus manual-only advances — no automated advance has ever occurred:

- clone at `f1dd41a8f0`, 2026-08-27 (539 commits behind current `origin/main`)
- manual `merge origin/main: Fast-forward` to `665d1d0480`, 2026-09-07 (135 behind current; was 130 behind at the recorded incident)
- manual fast-forwards on 2026-09-17 to `e5293bf5b1`, `e46d03aa83`, `5b143d9b15`, `4f12815e9a`, `71a719aef8`

Current HEAD `71a719aef8` matches local `origin/main` and the deploy markers — but only because of manual intervention, including mine earlier today.

## Implicated attestations, stated precisely

`f920-dc37-28e4-4a91` holds a valid `completion-verifier` signature at `verified-at-sha:e5293bf5b1...`, and `c65c-931c-ee39-4e63` one at `verified-at-sha:e46d03aa83...`. Ticket history records that the workspace had to be manually fast-forwarded to those SHAs before those closes could pass.

`f920` also carries a plan-review op-cert whose signed manifest anchors `verified-at-sha:5c2d3e664...` while the attestation plaintext `head_sha` reads `665d1d0480...`. `plan_review_status` now reports `stale-code` for it — but that verdict is computed from the locally available gate ref, not a remote fetch.

The distinction that matters: **the mechanism for a signed false PASS is demonstrated; an actual instance is not.** The observed `665d1d0480` incident produced a false FAIL, which is the safe direction. No attestation has been proven minted while the workspace was stale. A store-wide `verified-at-sha` census was attempted and cancelled for runtime, so that remains unestablished rather than ruled out.

## Fix direction

An operation-linked, in-process freshness boundary — not a GitHub-Actions-only trigger, which `project.portability` rejects. Shape: `fetch` + `merge --ff-only` on `MCP_CODE_DIR`, with dirty / diverged / unresolvable states failing loud and leaving the workspace untouched.

Wire it in both places, because they fail differently:

1. entrypoint / redeploy / no-op autodeploy tick — so drift cannot accumulate in the first place;
2. the gate path immediately before signing — so a stale workspace *refuses* rather than certifies.

(2) is the one that closes the correctness hole; (1) alone only shrinks the window. The gate check should report workspace HEAD, target SHA, and ahead/behind count, so a refusal is diagnosable rather than mysterious.

No changes were made. No AWS or Docker state was mutated. No LLM gate operation was run.

## Fix pushed for review as change 2988

`d31375d26a9` — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2988

**Scope held to the 3 files in `file_impact`:**

```
 infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md   |  41 +++++++
 infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh    |  50 ++++++++-
 tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py | 211 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
```

**What changed.** `provision_code()` no longer returns early for any present checkout. A clean workspace now fetches `origin main` and fast-forwards under the same directory lock the clone path already used. Dirty, diverged, and unreachable-remote states refuse and return non-zero without touching the workspace. Missing or unresolvable-HEAD checkouts still re-clone as before. Each refresh logs the HEAD SHA and the ahead/behind distance from `origin/main`, before and after.

**Startup behaviour on a refusal.** `provision_code` failure sets `rc=1` on `provision_store`, which normal startup backgrounds, so a dirty volume logs loudly and the server still starts. The refusal makes the stale tree visible rather than wedging the container — which matters, because wedging would convert this bug into an outage.

**TDD evidence.** The required first test failed for the right reason before any production change:

```
>       assert _head(checkout) == remote_tip, result.stderr
E       AssertionError: assert 'cbf508d29622...' == 'bf003333e76a...'
```

All 8 tests were mutation-checked and each one killed its mutant. `make lint` green, including actionlint.

Not yet voted. AC verification waits on the change landing and on a subsequent gate run reading a fresh tree.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The MCP server's code workspace is cloned once and never updated, so gates read a tree that drifts from `main` indefinitely.

The workspace is docker volume `gerrit_mcp_code`, mounted at `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` and passed as both `MCP_CODE_DIR` and `REBAR_ROOT` (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:390-417`). `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` treats a checkout as present when `.git` exists and `HEAD` resolves (`:127-130`), so `provision_code()` returns immediately for any present checkout (`:175-181`). Nothing ever fetches. `autodeploy.sh` advances a *separate* mirror at `/var/lib/rebar/mirror` (`:536-540`) and mounts this volume untouched (`:390-417`, `:852-960`).

So neither a container restart nor an image redeploy refreshes it. Once the clone succeeds, nothing in the system advances it again.

## Evidence

Reflog on `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` shows a clone at `f1dd41a8f0` (2026-08-27) and thereafter only manual fast-forwards. No automated advance has ever occurred.

At the recorded incident the volume was 130 commits behind `origin/main`, and closing `f920-dc37-28e4-4a91` failed with 6 criteria reporting work absent from the tree — work that had in fact merged. The verifier said so directly: "the current HEAD (665d1d0480...) does not contain these changes."

## Impact

A ticket whose work has genuinely merged cannot be closed, because the verifier cannot see it. The failure text invites the operator to re-record evidence or to `--force`, and both responses are wrong: the evidence is real and the tree is stale. Agents are forbidden from `--force`, so the correct-looking escape hatch is also unavailable.

The drift is unbounded and silent. Nothing reports it, and the gate output attributes the failure to the ticket rather than to the workspace.

## Approach

Refresh the workspace on the path that already owns its lifecycle, and make its drift observable instead of silent.

Add a refresh step to the provisioning path: take the existing checkout lock, require a clean tree, `git fetch origin main`, then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`. Run it for a checkout that is present, instead of returning early. A missing or unresolvable checkout keeps today's re-clone behaviour unchanged.

A dirty or diverged workspace is never mutated — it fails loud and is left exactly as found. Silently resetting a workspace a gate may be mid-read on would trade one correctness bug for another, and it matches the existing `fail-loud-no-auto-restart` posture.

The refresh emits the workspace SHA and its distance from the target, so drift is visible before it causes a confusing gate verdict rather than after.

**Portability.** The trigger is the MCP server's own lifecycle, which is where the workspace lives. That holds under any CI provider or none. A GitHub Actions workflow or a Gerrit hook as the only trigger would fail `project.portability`.

## Scope

- `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` — fetch and fast-forward an existing valid `MCP_CODE_DIR` rather than returning early.
- Tests for the refresh decisions.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — the workspace, how to check its drift, the manual fast-forward as break-glass.

## Testing strategy

TDD, failing test first in each case. Tests build a local repo whose `HEAD` is behind its remote and drive the provisioning path directly, with no container and no LLM call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A clean `MCP_CODE_DIR` behind `origin/main` is fast-forwarded to the remote tip. Verified by a test that fails against today's early-return provisioning.
- [ ] A dirty workspace is left byte-identical. Verified by comparing the working tree before the refusal against after it.
- [ ] A diverged workspace is left byte-identical. Verified the same way, against a non-fast-forwardable history.
- [ ] A refusal names its condition. Verified by asserting the failure text distinguishes dirty from diverged from unreachable.
- [ ] A missing workspace is still re-cloned as today. Verified by a test that removes the checkout.
- [ ] A workspace whose `HEAD` does not resolve is still re-cloned as today. Verified by a test that corrupts `HEAD`.
- [ ] An unreachable remote leaves the workspace untouched. Verified by pointing the remote at a nonexistent path.
- [ ] The refresh emits the workspace SHA with its distance from the target. Verified by reading the emitted diagnostics.
- [ ] The refresh requires no single CI provider. Verified by reading the trigger path for any GitHub Actions or Gerrit dependency.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` documents the workspace, the drift check, the break-glass. Verified by reading the file.

## Out of scope

The certified gates' ref pinning. While investigating this ticket it was noticed that the close path re-resolves its pinned SHA with `fetch=False`; whether that is a defect or the intended scope of that check has not been established, and no failure attributable to it has ever been observed. It is parked at P4 as `a2e5-094d-0736-456e` and is not a prerequisite for this work.

Also out of scope: the gates' verdict logic, and the separate `/var/lib/rebar/mirror` used by `autodeploy.sh`.

file_impact.reason: Provisioning path that returns early for any present checkout; gains the fetch and fast-forward
Tests for the refresh decisions: behind fast-forwards, dirty and diverged and unreachable refuse unmutated, missing and unresolvable re-clone
Documents the workspace, the drift check, and the manual fast-forward break-glass
